free_tier.stated: Developer plan, $0: 100 requests a day with no extra requests available; articles appear after a 24 hour delay and search reaches articles up to a month old.
free_tier.notes: A request returns up to 100 articles (pageSize maximum 100), each with content truncated to 200 characters; full article content is not offered on any plan. Browser CORS works only from localhost on this plan. The next plan up is Business at $449 a month for 250,000 requests.

per_object_cap.stated: 100 articles a request; article content truncated to 200 characters

retention.stated: search reaches articles up to a month old, and new articles appear after a 24 hour delay

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS; the key goes in the apiKey parameter, the X-Api-Key header or the Authorization header
chaining: A headline and article-metadata search: each result carries the article URL, and the full page is fetched separately by a crawler.

limits.value: 100 requests a day on the Developer plan; no extra requests on it
100 articles a request; content truncated to 200 characters
the rateLimited message sizes the Developer allowance as 100 requests over a 24 hour period, with 50 requests available every 12 hours
a Developer key reaches only the first 100 results of a query, however large totalResults is: a request for results past the 100th answers maximumResultsReached with HTTP 426

binding_note: 100 requests a day is met before anything else; the window behind the 429 rateLimited answer is not stated.

identity_cost.detail: The register form asks for a first name, an email that is verified (disposable addresses are blocked), a password, an individual or business choice, a reCAPTCHA check and acceptance of the terms; no card and no phone. One API key per holder at a time.

reliability_note: Too many requests in an unstated window answer HTTP 429 rateLimited, an exhausted key answers apiKeyExhausted, and the Developer plan has no uptime SLA.
confidence_note: Quota, delay, history window and register fields are read from first-party pages; a call with no key answered HTTP 401 apiKeyMissing, so the free key was not exercised. A call with a free key would move this to measured.
